Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

agecrypt is an R package implementing the age v1 file-encryption format through a vendored copy of the 0BSD C implementation agec. It encrypts and decrypts raw vectors, strings and files for X25519 recipients or with a scrypt passphrase, with optional ASCII armor. It has no external C library dependencies, draws randomness from the operating system, and interoperates with the reference age implementation. Hard R dependencies are zero; askpass is optional and used only for secure interactive prompting.

SSH keys, plugins, hardware recipients and post-quantum recipients require native stanza support and are intentionally out of scope. Do not add them as superficial R glue. The full out-of-scope list is in package-design.md.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-11: 0.1.1 is on CRAN, published 2026-10-21. main still carries Version: 0.1.1, with no .9000 bump yet. Planned but not built: encrypted R-object helpers, R connection streaming and an age_version() introspection function (package-design.md).

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #9 for v0.1.1, still open although 0.1.1 is published. Sibling packages that depend on this one: none recorded.

agecrypt has no cran-release.yaml, so CRAN-SUBMISSION is git-ignored and the release tag, GitHub release and .9000 bump are done by hand with pkg-post-cran. This is a deviation from .claude/shared/workflow.md.

Commands

Beyond the shared devtools commands:

Rscript -e 'pkgbuild::compile_dll()'              # rebuild src/ only
Rscript tools/gen-interop-fixtures.R              # regenerate interop fixtures
Rscript fuzz/gen-corpus.R                         # local fuzz corpus
fuzz/build.sh                                     # fuzz targets, ASan+UBSan
tools/update-vendored-agec.sh <ref> <full-sha>    # re-vendor agec

Regenerate the committed interoperability fixtures only when intentionally updating them; the command requires age or rage on PATH. fuzz/gen-corpus.R needs dev/agec and an installed package; see fuzz/README.md.

Architecture

R/ is organised by I/O shape (raw.R, text.R, file.R, passphrase.R, identity.R, recipients.R, conditions.R). src/binding.c holds the .Call entry points registered in src/init.c, which call the package-owned library core extracted from agec’s CLI (src/agec/agecore.c). Raw-vector operations go through negative virtual file descriptors in src/memio.c; file operations stream real descriptors in 64 KiB chunks through src/fileio.c. src/platform.c replaces upstream’s randomness. architecture.md has the details, the list of package-owned files and the Makevars layout.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Use age terminology and prefix public functions with age_.
  • Keep recipient and passphrase APIs as separate functions.
  • Raw APIs return raw vectors, including armored ciphertext.
  • File APIs stream through native file descriptors; do not load whole files into R vectors.
  • Every native entry point returns (status, payload). C must clean up and return an error suffix; it must not call Rf_error() mid-operation.
  • Keep native error suffixes aligned with the age_error_* R condition classes.
  • The backend is not reentrant. Run it on R’s main thread, one operation at a time.
  • Keep identity secrets in opaque, scrubbed native allocations. Do not print, coerce, or expose secret bytes. Key files are read and scrubbed in C: reading them in R interns the secret lines in R’s global string cache.
  • Never silently overwrite files or remove input/output collision checks.
  • Use operating-system CSPRNGs only. Compiled code must not call exit() or abort() or write to standard streams.
  • The reference age or rage CLI is a test oracle, never a runtime backend.
  • src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win list objects explicitly. Update both when compiled files change: their clean targets remove $(OBJECTS), so a stale list leaks object files into the source tarball. Keep all: $(SHLIB) as the first rule, or clean becomes make’s default goal, and preserve -iquote so agec’s io.h does not shadow the Windows system header.

Testing

  • Oracles. A curated subset of the C2SP CCTV vectors in tests/testthat/fixtures/vectors/, and fixtures produced by the reference age/rage CLI in tests/testthat/fixtures/interop/, which give reference-to-R coverage without a CLI at test time. Passphrase interoperability relies on the C2SP scrypt vectors, because the reference CLI reads passphrases from a TTY.
  • tests/testthat/helper-age.R provides new_pair() (a fresh identity and its recipient) and read_vector() (parses a CCTV-style fixture).
  • test-binding-hardening.R calls the registered native symbols directly: C must never crash, leak or reach undefined behaviour on bad input, with the R layer as defence in depth only.
  • For native changes, cover boundary sizes, authentication failures, cleanup paths, vectors, interoperability and fuzzing as applicable. The required behaviour matrix is in testing.md.

Continuous integration

  • R-CMD-check.yaml calls r-actions’ r-cmd-check.yml@v1; native-checks.yaml calls sanitizers, valgrind, lto, gctorture, rchk, analyzers and cran-special; coverage.yaml calls coverage.yml, pinned to a commit.
  • Both callers run quick on pull requests, full with the full-ci label, and full on every push to main, a deviation from .claude/shared/ci.md, whose callers run quick there. ASan and valgrind run only in the full profile, so a native change takes full-ci.
  • fuzz.yaml is the package’s own: libFuzzer under ASan+UBSan over the two decrypt targets, 120 s on pushes and pull requests that touch src/ or fuzz/, 900 s weekly. It gates with a paths filter rather than changes.yml.
  • pkgdown.yaml is r-lib’s example workflow, not an r-actions caller.
  • Valgrind suppressions in tools/valgrind.supp cover only leaks in third-party libraries loaded by the test suite, never agecrypt’s own code.

Vendored native code

Most files under src/agec/ are upstream agec sources (0BSD), including the transitive third-party code in src/agec/crypto/. Do not edit them opportunistically. Put upstreamable fixes on fix/* branches in pedrobtz/agec, import an immutable vendor-YYYY-MM-DD tag, and record all provenance and [package-only] changes in inst/COPYRIGHTS. The current snapshot is vendor-2026-09-30 on SourceHut 1.0.0; the update procedure is in vendoring-agec.md.
